#### What this PR does / why we need it:
In `completeRollingUpdate` function we should not compare `status.UpdatedReplicas` and `status.ReadyReplicas` with `status.Replicas` because `status.Replicas `is not showing total desired replicas, it shows only those replicas that are created, but here we want to compare with total desired replicas(set.Spec.Replicas) and only when `set.Spec.Replicas == status.ReadyReplicas` and `set.Spec.Replicas == status.UpdatedReplicas` we should change `status.CurrentReplicas` to `status.UpdatedReplicas`. This was causing updated image on pods with ordinal number lower than the rolling partition number when they were being deleted.

Issue is in all versions that have this PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117865 or has isCreated check when incrementing status.replicas.

Before making changes, and _especially_ before backporting them, we need to understand when the regression happened (what minor and what patch release) by seeing where the test fails. When we can see a working minor/patch and a broken minor/patch, then we can try to understand what changes went into the statefulset controller in that range and see how to restore previous functionality.

Without clearly understanding this, we're at risk for introducing new regressions trying to fix old regressions.

Collecting the relevant merges to master that changed statefulset behavior, along with the patch versions they were backported to, would help in understanding what we've regressed and how to recover

It's possible that *multiple* regressions have happened (e.g. something in 1.27.1 as initially reported in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119684, something else in 1.27.4 with backports of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119096, and something else in master with the recent merge of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120398). Rather than fixing forward, when dealing a regression, it is preferred to roll back (or at least partially revert) changes to get back to status quo for older release branches.

Timeline of changes and their impact:
- #115331 introduced a bug which caused StatefulSets to not recreate a pod completed successfully (bug: #118310). If the pods in test exited with code 0, they weren't recreated. This probably prevented the detection of current bug (recreating at wrong revision, which was introduced later) in e2e tests. **Versions: 1.28.0, 1.27.0**
- #117865 introduced another bug: `status.Replicas` is updated with a delay - it's showing too small value immediately after the pods are created (not counting them), but self-correcting the next time the object is processed (bug: #120732). Semantics of `status.Replicas` remained unchanged: all existing (created and not deleted) pods. **Versions: 1.28.0, 1.27.4, 1.26.7, 1.25.12**
- While the test was passing (not detecting the second issue), a consequence of miscalculated status was reported in #119684 and #119685: we rely on this value to complete rolling update. The first attempt to fix it (removing `IsCreated()` check)  *would change the semantics of `status.Replicas`*, overestimating the number of replicas: #119759. 
- #120398 fixed the issue with not recreating a pod. This caused the test to fail (bug: #120700) and detect the issue with pods recreated at wrong revision. We can roll it back and merge again later, if getting tests to green is a priority - I believe this will just conceal the bug with wrong revision again.
- This PR (#120731, in case this is referenced elsewhere) is the second attempt to fix the issue with wrong revision: it doesn't use `status.Replicas` to determine rolling update progress, but rather `spec.Replicas`. I believe this is more resilient, since it's a perfectly valid for `status.Replica` to be lower or higher than desired replicas temporarily. If we ever reached complete rolling update check in such state, we'd be dealing with the same issue again. I recognise a lot of StatefulSet controller logic is based on such invariants, but I believe it's safer to check the actual conditions needed to safely complete rollback.
- We should definitely also fix `status.Replicas` calculation (bug: #120732), however we don't yet have a PR with this fix.
- Finally, I believe the failing test is likely accepting a pod in `Succeeded` phase as having the correct revision. (This is speculation as I haven't digged into this test - @mimowo might have more context). If so, this test would be more robust if it only considered running pods.

We are no longer convinced this PR introduced the bug. The issue is reproducible in 1.27.0, which doesn't have it.

I'm trying to understand it better as the hypothesis "we are just miscalculating newly created pods" just got much weaker:
- the bug happens in some versions before the change to calculating status (1.27.0-1.27.3 confirmed)
- the bug is indeterministic. If the problem was due to creating pods and completing rolling update in the same iteration, I believe the bug would have been deterministic (at least unless an error occurs and ends the iteration prematurely).
- the "newly created pod not counted" scenario implies that the pod has already been created _before_ the complete upgrade check. This could cause the upgrade to complete prematurely, but the pod would have been created _before_ this completion, so it should still be at the current revision. Only deleting it a second time could trigger the creation at updated revision.

What we do know:
- changing rolling update check to use `set.spec.Replicas` fixes the issue -> the error happens due to comparison with `status.Replicas`
- counting all replicas (previous fix attempt) also prevents this issue, even though it changes the semantics of status -> we are probably not counting some pods in `status.Replicas`

The only situation where we don't count some pods is when they have empty pod phase. We've assumed so far that this can only happen if the pod was created in the same iteration. I'm going to run some more experiments to verify this.

So we may still complete rolling upgrade (and I believe we do) if we exit `updateStatefulSet` with error: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L118

When the StatefulSet observes a pod in `Failed` phase, it'll try to recreate it. On 1.26.0, this works immediately in a kind cluster. On 1.27.0, the pod is deleted successfully, but the create call fails for a while with `object is being deleted: pods "web-am-0" already exists, the server was not able to generate a unique name for the object`, then succeeds. 

On both versions after a single failed create call, we exit with error and a non-nil status with `Replicas=1` (we never increased the counter as the create failed). Because status isn't nil, we proceed to `updateStatefulSetStatus`, where we do the complete rolling upgrade check.

[Pod Lifecycle](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/) documentation suggests what may have triggered this to occur somewhat reliably in 1.27.0: pods linger in Failed/Succeeded phase before being deleted from the API server:
>Since Kubernetes 1.27, the kubelet transitions deleted Pods, except for [static Pods](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/static-pod/) and [force-deleted Pods](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-termination-forced) without a finalizer, to a terminal phase (Failed or Succeeded depending on the exit statuses of the pod containers) before their deletion from the API server.

This also explains indeterminism, and particularly @soltysh's results with the bug occurring more rarely when there are 3 master nodes instead of 1 - it probably increases latency sufficiently for a pod to not be caught in "failed, but not yet really deleted state" as often.

So the bug is probably very long standing, and it's triggered by a failed create call for the pod 0 when partition=1 and other pods are already updated. That's _very_ specific and even if observed before 1.27, would have been hard to reproduce without simulating API server failure for this specific call. 

We can verify this hypothesis by trying to force delete the pod and checking if (as per documentation) it's deleted immediately and prevents the error from occurring.

(Actually, there's a possibility that this could have failed for more pods than pod 0, if all current replicas were deleted at once and the first create call failed. I don't think it changes much as it's even more unlikely to occur than for a single pod.)

Exiting with error and status values that correspond to reality, then updating the actual status based on it seems reasonable - we may have changed something at this point, although it probably wouldn't hurt to skip complete rolling upgrade check if we exit with an error. Checking `status.Replicas` instead of `set.Spec.Replicas` is the questionable part - why should we rely on this value, which may be lower or higher than desired replicas, is unclear to me. I agree it makes sens to still check it - to make sure there are no extra pods - but what we really need to be looking at here is desired replicas.

>Second, I think the issue isn't with delaying the deletion, either with graceful termination, or finalizers. I think the issue occurs when the pod is deleted completely, so the status.Replicas is 2, as the field counts any existing pods: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L324-L326.

The issue also occurs in 1.27.0 (before the linked code was submitted).

What happens then:
- we count the pod as created: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L317
- we decrease the number of replicas on deletion of failed pod: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L414
- we replace the pod in `replicas` slice with the new one (without phase == not created): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L416
- we fail to create a pod _and never increase replicas again_: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L434
